name: MarkLab capability map
scope: Complete major capability and mathematical-family inventory for this checkout, with concrete inputs, outputs, command routes, interactions and research uses. Individual Rust helpers and every estimator option are not enumerated. The research examples are possible study designs, not validated clinical claims.

reading_guide.slide_to_research: Start here: what a slide can become and which steps require upstream tools or explicit joins.
reading_guide.exploratory_slide_analysis: Recommended discovery sequence, useful first outputs, branch choices and limits of single-slide evidence.
reading_guide.capabilities: Full major-family inventory. Each entry retains its calculations, input, output, wiring, uses, limits and source locations.
reading_guide.mathematical_methods: Named mathematical constructions and equations, including Bayesian, Fourier, graph, spatial, fusion, information and dynamical methods.
reading_guide.multimodal_integration: How H-optimus-like patch vectors, CellViT-like cell vectors/classes, measured markers and spatial features can be combined.
reading_guide.interactions: Implemented chains versus combinations requiring explicit user orchestration; output JSONs are not universally interchangeable.
reading_guide.applications: Representative scientific questions and the capabilities to combine.
reading_guide.command_index: Source-declared public leaf commands grouped by prefix. Run marklab <prefix> <command> --help for the actual required arguments. Help/private worker entrypoints are excluded.
reading_guide.sources: Repository-relative paths. Existing scientific evidence is reported with its scope, not claimed to have been rerun for this document.

slide_to_research.starting_point: A raw WSI provides pixels and metadata. The general analysis starts after cells, marks, geometry or embeddings have been measured upstream and mapped to explicit contracts.

operations: External segmentation, phenotype/marker measurement, region annotation and optional image encoders
stages.output: Cell table; observation window with holes; optional region/nucleus polygons, cell/patch vectors and measured assay channels
stages.wiring: WSI access is native; segmentation, encoder inference and most native model-export parsing are external.

stages.input: Measured objects, IDs, coordinate frames and producer declarations
operations: Validate units, identity joins, missingness and observation/prediction status
Register sections if measurements come from different physical sections
stages.output: Aligned objects with a declared window, patient hierarchy and uncertainty
stages.wiring: Supported adapters and registration workflows are native; an unsupported export needs explicit mapping.

stages.input: Calibrated cells, marks, vectors and optional structures
operations: Counts, density, class composition and QC
Spatial curves, mark/Fourier spectra, graphs and selected structure descriptors
stages.output: Physical-coordinate maps, curves, local measurements and slide/region summaries
stages.wiring: Multiple native workflows; no single command automatically runs every family.

stages.input: A focused question plus compatible measurements
operations: Factor models or patient-level ridge/kernel/predictive fusion
Topology/transport, longitudinal, causal or simulation models when supported by the study design
stages.output: Effects, posterior summaries, latent representations, held-out predictions or mechanistic hypotheses
stages.wiring: Explicit model-specific requests; arbitrary preceding output files need a declared transformation/join.

stages.input: Defined endpoints and independent patients/sites, or a justified experimental/time-course design
operations: Nested patient evaluation and external validation
Model checks, sensitivity and validation appropriate to the question
stages.output: Study-level effects and uncertainty, honest performance estimates and limits
stages.wiring: study and selected pathology workflows integrate aggregation; other endpoint families require explicit patient reduction.

possible_deliverables: Density, phenotype, neighborhood, marker and interface maps
Distance, spatial-frequency, graph and topology signatures
Model-specific posterior effects and diagnostic reports
Synthetic fields or patterns for hypothesis and method testing
not_inferred_from_one_slide: Cell communication, force or causation from spatial association alone

exploratory_slide_analysis.recommendation: Begin with a calibrated descriptive tissue map, then pursue a small number of spatial questions suggested by visible structure. Preserve a separate patient/site validation stage for any generalizable claim.
minimum_input: Physical coordinates and observed tissue window including holes
Patient/slide identity and explicit sampling/region selection
Cell classes or a declared measured/probabilistic mark
Upstream segmentation/measurement QC; optional annotations, axes and embedding vectors
first_outputs: Counts, area, density, class fractions and missingness by analyzed region
Spatial overlay of cells/classes/marker values against tissue and exclusions
Neighborhood composition or class-pair co-occurrence at a few justified physical scales
One focused organization analysis: a mark spectrum, cross-type curve, continuous-field autocorrelation or interface profile
Effect-size/curve plots plus support and availability, not only p-values

sequence.detail: Inspect cell placement, calibration, duplicate/missing values, segmentation/class confidence, annotation alignment and window holes on the image. Choose representative ROIs without selecting solely on an extreme downstream statistic.

Start with density, class composition, neighborhood composition and relevant marker/annotation profiles. pathology maps is a natural first branch when its marker/class/annotation recipe fits the data; architecture additionally needs supplied region/nuclear geometry.

sequence.action: Pick a few interpretable scale questions
sequence.detail: Use marked analyze for an eligible binary/probability table; co-occurrence/enrichment or directed cross-g for classes; Moran/variograms for measured fields. Add unmarked K/L and G/F/J if crowding/voids is the question and the input/edge support is appropriate.

Check density, tissue compartments, distance to structures, edge effects and regional strata before interpreting a class association. Compare only a small justified set of null/intensity/scale choices.

Use Fourier for scale/direction; nematic order for measured axes; graph/topology for connectivity; embeddings/factors for representation; Bayesian models for a stated observation/process model. Choose by the question rather than running every command.
Record the marker pair, region, radii, grid, graph and model choices that led to a candidate. A p-value from the chosen run does not account for every unrecorded alternative inspected.
Repeat on held-out patients or sites. Fit preprocessing/tuning inside training patients. Use the declared patient-level multiplicity family and preserve pairing, blocks and sites.

branch_guide.next: co-occurrence/enrichment and directed cross-g; inspect density/compartment and label-null sensitivity
annotation-distance profiles, Moran/variograms and eligible local maps; scan only with its repeat-the-search null
marked spectrum/anisotropy; architecture and nematic axes where measured; unmarked hyperuniformity only on its valid rectangular support

branch_guide.signal: Distinct morphology in cell or patch features
branch_guide.next: embedding semivariograms/cross-covariance and shared factors; patient ridge/kernel comparisons only when independent targets are available
connectivity/persistence, graph spectra, compartment contact and lacunarity with resolution sensitivity
a declared point-process or dynamical model with posterior-predictive/simulation checks and temporal/perturbation evidence where needed

exploratory_slide_analysis.single_slide_limit: A single slide can generate a spatial hypothesis and quantify within-window structure. Millions of cells do not create independent patient replication; supervised performance and population claims need the corresponding held-out cohort design.

references.supports: Official example places QC and spatial visualization before neighborhood/spatial statistics; not a Marklab interoperability or estimator-parity claim.
Model-selection optimization can bias evaluation on the same finite data; supports separating tuning from held-out assessment.

interfaces.rust: marklab root exports plus spatial, structure, marks, autocorrelation, compartments, embeddings, workflow, pathology and backend modules; companion crates expose additional scientific APIs.
interfaces.cli: marklab with the cli Cargo feature; defaults also enable parallel, csv and parquet.
interfaces.python_client: Thin subprocess client for multiplex studies and pathology architecture; explicit cell-table, AnnData and selected upstream adapters. Not a Python binding for every Rust API.
interfaces.python_workers: Selected model, registration, topology and prediction commands use the repository's locked Python 3.12 runtime.

optional_features.wsi: Slide metadata and bounded RGBA region reading via wsi-rs.
optional_features.parquet: Cell-table Parquet and strict embedding Arrow IPC/Parquet profiles.
optional_features.csv: Cell tables and normalized CSV adapters.

shared_contracts.identity: Explicit patient/site/specimen/block/core/slide/section/region/cell/patch/timepoint IDs, hierarchy and replication roles; coordinates and measurements stay bound to their objects.
shared_contracts.coordinates: Declared physical units, coordinate frames, axis/image conventions and transforms; no implicit pixel-to-micrometre conversion or registration.
shared_contracts.observations: Binary, probability, categorical, ordinal, continuous, assay and vector marks; missingness and measured/imported-prediction/morphology-prediction/derived-summary status remain explicit.
shared_contracts.geometry: Observation-window polygons/multipolygons can preserve holes and disconnected pieces; each method has its own geometry and edge-correction restrictions.
shared_contracts.inference: Null model, exchangeability unit, strata, support, seed and multiplicity family are part of the scientific design. Random labeling, fixed-count spatial simulations and model-based posterior prediction answer different questions.
shared_contracts.availability: Unavailable/disabled/failed/nonconverged values have explicit status or errors; missing results are not scientific zeros.
shared_contracts.reproducibility: Fixed inputs, settings, seed, implementation and numerical environment support replay; universal cross-platform bitwise identity is not claimed.
shared_contracts.resources: Method-specific input, memory, work, graph, geometry, simulation and worker-time budgets; admission estimates are not measured performance guarantees.
shared_contracts.publication: Analysis/study directories publish transactionally. Utilities have their own file contracts. Durable projects reuse compatible completed results and invalidate dependent work when inputs change.
shared_contracts.results: The current root result.json contract is 0.5; its reader accepts the current version. Specialized methods have separate versioned documents. This inventory changes no result format.

does: Bounded materialized AnnData/H5AD including sparse round trips
Optional normalized CellViT CSV/NPY and bundle profiles
input_adapters.input: Upstream cells, annotations or vectors plus IDs, calibration, window, patient grouping and producer declarations.
input_adapters.output: Validated patterns, study slides, architecture recipes or embedding artifacts.
input_adapters.used_by: analyze/classical/batch, multimodal, study, pathology architecture and embedding workflows; adapters are specific contracts, not universal native-format readers.
uses: Analyze outputs from a chosen segmentation/embedding model
Normalize multiplex platforms into a common patient-level study
input_adapters.limits: AnnData backed/lazy arrays are unsupported. QuPath nucleus and architecture profiles differ. Generic embeddings do not require CellViT's dimension/calibration. Explicit mapping is required for unsupported native exports.

whole_slide_access.input: Supported WSI file and explicit scene/level/plane/region.
whole_slide_access.output: Metadata JSON or decoded region pixels/image.
uses: Extract regions for external image processing or visual review
whole_slide_access.limits: No WSI writer, cell segmentation, viewer-state import or general OME-XML semantic/calibration adapter. Public pixel agreement is scoped to the tested Aperio region.

does: Permutation-whitened mark spectrum and low-frequency excess
Tapered FFT periodogram and scale-energy curves
Multiscale residual maps and connected territories
marked_section.input: Cell coordinates, binary/probabilistic marks, tissue mask and TOML configuration; declared scalar API additionally binds identity/status/provenance.
marked_section.output: Marked-pattern JSON with primary endpoint, curves/envelopes, territories, QC and availability; configurable Parquet curves, GeoJSON territories, figures and run manifest.
marked_section.used_by: AnalysisEngine -> analyze/batch -> OutputWriter; marked workflow nodes and pre/post DAG reuse the same engine. Internal spectral helpers are not separate supported public modules.
uses: Detect clustered, dispersed or directional labeling
Check whether spatial strata explain a label pattern
marked_section.limits: Conditions on observed cell geometry and declared exchangeability; a significant label pattern does not establish clonality or cause. Each curve envelope covers its own eligible scale family, not every marker/run.

does: Marked pre/post endpoint and curve comparisons
prepost_and_batch.input: Manifest rows or compatible completed pre/post analyses, with matching scientific identities and settings.
prepost_and_batch.output: Per-analysis outputs or change/comparison summaries with availability and margin assessments.
prepost_and_batch.used_by: batch, prepost, multimodal batch/prepost; Rust comparison functions; project marked-prepost and marked pre/post DAG.
prepost_and_batch.limits: Sections contain different cells; this is not cell tracking or evidence of a treatment effect. Population inference requires a patient-level design.

does: Homogeneous K/L with border, translation or isotropic correction
Homogeneous g with standard, translation or isotropic correction
Nearest-neighbor G, empty-space F and J
point_patterns_2d.input: 2-D points, exact observed window, radii/bins, edge policy and optional types/intensities/compartments; declared simulation or labeling null.
point_patterns_2d.output: Radius-indexed curves, pair/support counts, intensity diagnostics and optional envelopes/p-values.
point_patterns_2d.used_by: marklab::spatial; classical/nearest-space; project spatial routes; pathology spatial-study. Global envelopes use marklab-numerics.
point_patterns_2d.limits: CSR relocates cells; random labeling fixes them. Inhomogeneous cross-K is not implemented. Edge/normalization conventions matter; single-type inhomogeneous g lacks independent reference agreement. Public agreement applies to documented observed estimators, not every inferential configuration.

does: Categorical enrichment with exact fixed-count null moments and Monte Carlo inference
Soft neighborhood composition at one or multiple radii
categorical_marks.input: Aligned typed marks, cell IDs/coordinates/frame, levels or complete probability simplex, radius and declared null/support semantics.
categorical_marks.output: Co-occurrence/mixing matrices, compositions/diversity, weighted pair curves, bounds or permutation inference.
categorical_marks.used_by: marklab::marks and exported workflow nodes; numerics categorical-co-occurrence/enrichment and project categorical-pair expose selected methods. Most soft/ordinal methods are library building blocks; soft neighborhoods feed pathology maps.
uses: Retain uncertainty when only top-1 probabilities are available
categorical_marks.limits: Complete-simplex analyses require complete probabilities; top-1 bounds do not invent them. Co-occurrence is descriptive; enrichment count/moment agreement does not validate every Monte Carlo/null design. No learned niche clustering.

does: Continuous product-weighted K and unweighted baseline
KSG mutual information with permutation, block or variogram-matching spatial null
continuous_and_probability_marks.input: Finite aligned scalar/probability marks and spatial design; mutual information takes two measurements and its null settings.
continuous_and_probability_marks.output: Weighted curves, dependence summaries, envelopes/p-values or MI/null effect summaries.
continuous_and_probability_marks.used_by: marklab::marks and method-specific AnalysisNode types; numerics mutual-information. Probability marks also feed the marked-section spectrum.
uses: Nonlinear dependence between two cell measurements
continuous_and_probability_marks.limits: Probabilities, continuous values and hard labels have distinct contracts. Spatial MI can reflect shared regional context; reference/calibration evidence is scoped and includes a documented tie-breaking mismatch.

does: Unique information from each source and synergistic information
Target-specific information and marginal/joint mutual information in bits
partial_information_decomposition.input: Declared target/source levels and definitions, positive joint counts, statistical unit and state/count bounds.
partial_information_decomposition.output: Empirical information decomposition, target entropy, observed support and target-specific terms.
uses: Explore information complementarity between two prespecified low-dimensional representations
Check copy, XOR and independent controls before interpreting a tissue table
partial_information_decomposition.limits: No automatic binning, bias correction, confidence interval or causal interpretation. I_min compares information amounts: independent source bits copied into a joint target receive one redundant and one synergistic bit.

does: Global Moran I and Geary C
Local multivariate Moran with locationwise and global Max-T inference
Scalar empirical semivariogram and ERL envelope
Binary, including-isolates and row-standardized weight policies
autocorrelation_and_variograms.input: Scalar marks or complete multivariate rows, fixed points/window, radius or lag bins, weights, optional strata and permutations.
autocorrelation_and_variograms.output: Global/local association, null expectations, p-values, corrected local tests or lag/pair/semivariance curves.
autocorrelation_and_variograms.used_by: marklab::autocorrelation; study and pathology maps; numerics local-multivariate-moran; project local-multivariate-moran/scalar-variogram.
autocorrelation_and_variograms.limits: Local whole-row unconditional shuffling and population variance differ from default conditional LISA. Prespecify scaling/radius/strata. Public cohort evidence is scoped to binary symmetric weights including isolates.

does: Region-specific intensity for K/L and g
compartments.input: Window and nonoverlapping compartment polygons in one frame; aligned histologic labels and radius where cells are used.
compartments.output: Interface profiles, mixing/contact fractions, fragmentation and compartment-conditioned spatial summaries.
compartments.used_by: marklab::compartments and workflow nodes; project piecewise-compartment methods and pathology spatial-study share partition geometry. Pathology maps separately profiles supplied annotations using common window geometry.
compartments.limits: Regions/classes are supplied upstream. Fragmentation alone cannot report cell mixing. Synthetic geometry and scoped SPIAT mixing agreement do not establish cohort performance.

does: Ordinary kriging with declared exponential/spherical/Gaussian variogram and block-held-out checks
Landy-Szalay pair excess from a declared random catalog
Mapper graph with one-dimensional lens, overlapping cover and single-link clusters
Unmarked rectangular-window structure factor, H and alpha
structure_descriptors.input: Points, scalar fields, vectors or binary masks with declared window/pixel size, scale grid, lens, variogram or random catalog as applicable.
structure_descriptors.output: Dispersion, field predictions/variance, orientation order, scaling/gap summaries, excess-pair curve, Mapper graph or structure-factor descriptors.
structure_descriptors.used_by: marklab::structure and numerics descriptor commands; scalar variograms can inform a user-declared kriging model, but there is no automatic variogram fitting.
structure_descriptors.limits: Kriging assumes constant mean/stationary isotropy. Mapper has a 1-D lens and no stability inference. H/alpha lack uncertainty and require a fully observed rectangle. Descriptive scaling is not proof of fractality/hyperuniformity. Mark spectra and unmarked structure factors are distinct.

does: Weighted global and local axial Q tensor, scalar order S and director
Regular-grid director field with complete circular support
Resolved +1/2 and -1/2 defects from doubled-phase plaquette winding
nematic_orientation.input: Oriented cells with positive weights, physical coordinates, observation window, local/grid scales, order and branch thresholds, and work limits.
nematic_orientation.output: Global/local/grid estimates, support/availability, every plaquette status and resolved half-defect counts.
uses: Map aligned versus disordered nuclear or cell axes
Compare orientation structure with invasive-front distance or declared architecture
nematic_orientation.limits: Axial angles identify theta and theta+pi. Low order, incomplete support, holes, boundaries and branch ambiguity remain unresolved. Static geometry does not measure forces.

does: H&E/IHC cell matching and fused-cell records
multimodal_registration_and_neighborhood.input: H&E classes, IHC measurements, calibrated sections/windows and corresponding landmarks.
multimodal_registration_and_neighborhood.output: Registration/fusion diagnostics, graph-neighborhood summaries, interaction curves and territory outputs.
multimodal_registration_and_neighborhood.used_by: MultimodalEngine -> multimodal analyze/batch -> multimodal prepost. Factor-model commands below are separate workflows, not automatic stages of analyze.
multimodal_registration_and_neighborhood.limits: Registration and matching uncertainty can affect every downstream statistic. Neighborhood adjacency does not prove signaling or biological cell identity.

does: Per-marker Moran I and Geary C
Equal patient weighting after slide means
multiplex_study.input: Study recipe with numeric/binary/categorical channels, slides, windows, patient/group IDs, radius/weight policy and inference design.
multiplex_study.output: Cached slide/patient results plus result.json, report.md and manifest.
multiplex_study.used_by: study run/describe; Python run_study; Rust analyze/execute/publish_multiplex_study.
uses: Compare spatial protein organization between patient groups
multiplex_study.limits: Categorical channels are retained but not treated as numeric autocorrelation marks. Missing marker values alter the analyzed graph. Unavailable required slide results suppress that marker's patient test. Experimental scope is the documented binary-symmetric-including-isolates design.

pathology_maps.input: Calibrated cell markers/phenotypes, observation windows, supplied annotations and declared radii/distance bands.
pathology_maps.output: JSON/report plus per-slide SVG and per-cell GeoJSON map layers.
pathology_maps.used_by: pathology maps; Rust analyze_pathology_maps/publish_pathology_maps compose clipped annotation-offset geometry, soft-neighborhood composition and local Moran.
uses: Local Ki67 or other marker hotspots
pathology_maps.limits: Annotations and measurements are supplied upstream. Local maps are within-slide summaries, not independent patient observations.

does: Patient cell-type fractions and area-normalized density
Geometric balances and amalgamated log ratios
Joint patient Max-T and within-group bootstrap intervals
pathology_composition.input: Typed cells, patient/group/slide IDs, windows, declared log-ratio groups and grid designs.
pathology_composition.output: Patient and contrast tables, grid GeoJSON, MAUP SVG, JSON and report.
pathology_composition.used_by: pathology composition pools counts/areas across each patient's slides before group inference.
uses: Separate relative composition from absolute density
Check whether regional heterogeneity depends on sampling-grid choices
pathology_composition.limits: No automatic pseudocounts for zeros. Unavailable endpoints are excluded from the family without silently dropping patients. Marginal bootstrap intervals are not simultaneous intervals.

does: Intensity-adjusted L-r, g-1 and directed cross-g-1
Gaussian plug-in or refitted simulation nulls
Area-weighted patient curves and functional group tests
pathology_spatial_study.input: Typed cells/windows, patient/group declarations, common radii, intensity/edge/null/support settings and optional compartment geometry.
pathology_spatial_study.output: Slide/patient curves, null-curves.json, curve plots, JSON and report; separate within-slide, across-slide and patient-group inference.
pathology_spatial_study.used_by: pathology spatial-study composes spatial intensity, pair statistics, simulation envelopes and cohort curve inference.
uses: Compare patient groups' clustering after accounting for density
pathology_spatial_study.limits: Spatial simulations condition on counts; theoretical Poisson reference curves are not the finite-count null. No dropping or interpolating unsupported radii/patients. Fixed-bandwidth rectangular observed L-r has Experimental evidence; other configurations remain Research.

does: Cell-centered circular search across declared radii
pathology_scan.input: Target phenotype, eligible cells, strata, windows and prespecified scan radii.
pathology_scan.output: Best circle per slide, enrichment/test results, strata tables, SVG/GeoJSON, JSON and report.
pathology_scan.used_by: pathology scan searches and re-searches within each slide; it does not perform a patient-group hotspot comparison.
uses: Detect unusually concentrated immune or abnormal-cell regions
pathology_scan.limits: Only the best qualifying circle is tested; secondary clusters are not. A scan circle is not a lesion boundary, and may span disconnected tissue.

does: Invasive-front derivation with exclusions and declared-front distance agreement
Signed front-distance bands and exact region overlap areas
ITBCC-style budding candidates, front-constrained hotspot and Bd grade
Cell attachment and spatial-transcriptomic spot coverage fractions
pathology_architecture.input: Calibrated tissue/epithelium/architecture-region polygons, provenance, optional lumen/mucin/front layers, epithelial cell labels/nuclear measurements and registered circular spots.
pathology_architecture.output: Component/band/cell/spot tables, front/bulk GeoJSON and complete JSON result.
pathology_architecture.used_by: pathology architecture; Rust analyze/publish; Python QuPath annotation conversion and run_pathology_architecture. Spot IDs provide an explicit join to external expression/protein tables.
uses: Quantify glandular/solid/fragmented architecture along an invasive front
Compare morphology and registered cell states
Describe mixed tissue coverage of capture spots
pathology_architecture.limits: No epithelial segmentation or class prediction. Region overlap uses geometric areas; whole-component class uses its interior point. Budding depends on supplied components/nuclei and lacks pathologist validation. Nuclear alignment is a shape descriptor, not a force measurement.

embedding_artifacts_and_scales.input: Externally generated finite vectors, exact object links, coordinates/footprints, source declarations and optional overlap weights.
embedding_artifacts_and_scales.output: Bound and verified multiscale embedding artifacts, linkage/QC and dispersion summaries.
embedding_artifacts_and_scales.used_by: marklab::embeddings and marklab-embeddings; verified artifact graphs feed cell/patch/region analysis rather than relying on row position alone.
uses: Connect morphology features across cell, patch and slide scales
Avoid counting overlapping patches as independent support
Preserve exact identity during vector import and aggregation
embedding_artifacts_and_scales.limits: No encoder inference/training. Internal columnar profiles intentionally reject arbitrary Arrow/Parquet schemas. Aggregation requires explicit support and producer declarations.

does: Embedding-feature and cross-modal covariance by distance
Embedding kernels and kernel mark correlation
embedding_spatial_analysis.input: Identity-aligned cell/patch vectors, coordinates, distance bins or kernels, mark/morphology values and declared support/splits.
embedding_spatial_analysis.output: Spatial curves, covariance matrices, kernel artifacts, contrasts, dispersion metrics or ranked analogous regions.
embedding_spatial_analysis.used_by: marklab::embeddings and marklab-embeddings::analysis; bayes embedding commands expose descriptive computations as well as models; selected project routes add caching.
uses: Compare morphology with measured protein patterns
Assess which spatial scales carry feature dependence
embedding_spatial_analysis.limits: A bayes command prefix does not imply Bayesian inference. Unweighted observed vector semivariograms have scoped Experimental agreement; other extensions remain Research. Vector dimensions/features and preprocessing must be comparable.

does: Spatial latent factors with dense GP or SPDE prior
Dropout-robust factors and joint pathology models
Patient-level nested ridge comparisons of baseline/cell/patch/neighborhood/measured features
multimodal_factor_and_complementarity_mo.input: Declared aligned modality matrices/tensors, hierarchy/spatial support, missingness and patient training/held-out design.
multimodal_factor_and_complementarity_mo.output: Factors/loadings, shared variation, model diagnostics or held-out complementarity comparisons.
multimodal_factor_and_complementarity_mo.used_by: multimodal model commands; multimodal compare-models and bayes test-cell-patch-complementarity; durable project counterpart for complementarity.
uses: Test whether cells and patches add distinct predictive information
Compare feature scales under patient-held-out evaluation
multimodal_factor_and_complementarity_mo.limits: Separate from multimodal analyze; no automatic factor fitting in the basic registration workflow. Factors are not validated cell states, learned niches or causal mechanisms.

does: Training-only feature standardization and centered unit-mean-diagonal linear/RBF kernels
Finite simplex-grid modality weights and ridge selection inside nested patient folds
Equal-weight and each single-modality baseline on the same outer folds
learned_multimodal_kernels.input: One complete row per patient, modality feature names and kernel settings, continuous target, explicit inner/outer folds, ridge candidates and work/memory bounds.
learned_multimodal_kernels.output: Held-out predictions, RMSE/MAE, fold weights and selected ridge penalties, inactive modalities and estimated resource use.
uses: Compare patch, cell, composition and spatial feature similarities without concatenating raw vectors
Test whether multimodal similarity predicts a declared endpoint beyond each source alone
learned_multimodal_kernels.limits: Finite grid search, not a continuous optimizer or Bayesian posterior. No encoder inference, automatic patient pooling, imputation, classification/survival likelihood, interval estimation or deployed full-cohort model. Weights are not causal importance.

does: Laplacian spectral basis and frequency-band energies
Dirichlet energy, permutation smoothness and local embedding roughness
graph_analysis.input: Declared weighted graphs/signals or physical points/radius; optional edge types, hyperedges, triangles/incidence, strata and perturbations.
graph_analysis.output: Operators, spectra, energies, diffused signals, multiscale features, stability, motifs, group centrality or signal decompositions.
graph_analysis.used_by: marklab-graph; graph commands; bayes graph-signal/embedding commands; selected sparse/signal/motif project routes. graph validate exercises mathematical oracles.
graph_analysis.limits: Graph construction is part of the hypothesis. No individual betweenness or learned niche/community model. Observed group scores have Experimental evidence; other graph features remain Research and lack calibrated tissue-cohort interpretation.

topology.input: Physical points or persistence diagrams with patient labels; masks/pixel size/connectivity; declared filtrations, landmarks and perturbations.
topology.output: Simplices and birth/death pairs, diagram summaries/comparisons, stability distances, mask morphology or connectivity transitions.
topology.used_by: marklab-topology types/native connectivity; topology CLI orchestrates GUDHI persistence and scikit-image morphology workers; witness workflows have project routes.
uses: Connected clusters and loops across scales
Patient-level comparison of declared topological features
topology.limits: GUDHI is the persistence implementation, not an independent validation oracle. Features are not automatically anatomical structures or biomarkers; pixel conventions affect raster topology.

nonrigid_registration.input: Images or corresponding landmarks with explicit frames/spacing, deformation settings and uncertainty model.
nonrigid_registration.output: Transforms/deformations, alignment and uncertainty diagnostics or registered atlas.
nonrigid_registration.used_by: registration commands use Python workers; separate spatial3d workflows explicitly propagate registration uncertainty into serial/longitudinal K analyses.
uses: Assess how registration affects spatial conclusions
nonrigid_registration.limits: Correspondence is assumed or modeled. Deformation alone cannot distinguish biological change from cutting/mounting artifacts.

does: Registered longitudinal voxel-K change with deformation/control draws
spatial_3d.input: Calibrated 3-D points, cuboid/voxel window and spacing, types/intensities/uncertainty; advanced workflows add section registration, transforms, draws or clone records.
spatial_3d.output: K/cross curves, voxel geometry, spatial graph, registered-volume/change diagnostics, alpha topology or clone-location contrasts.
spatial_3d.used_by: marklab-spatial3d; flat spatial3d CLI routes; project caches four principal K workflows. Registered analyses run the same voxel K engine after declared coordinate mapping.
spatial_3d.limits: No independent 3-D K comparison or validated serial-section patient cohort. Window must represent actual observation. Registration draws/controls are explicit inputs; no same-cell tracking or causal change claim. Bayesian GP inverse-square anisotropy output cannot directly serve as dimensionless K anisotropy.

does: Functional L2 permutation and simultaneous equivalence
Multisite fixed/REML random-effects synthesis and covariate contrasts
Patient-nested field reduction and Max-T calibration
cohort_inference.input: Declared patient endpoints or curves plus groups, pairs, blocks, clusters, sites, covariates, hierarchy and prespecified margins where applicable.
cohort_inference.output: Effects, p-values/adjusted families, uncertainty intervals, heterogeneity/sensitivity, distances and patient summaries.
cohort_inference.used_by: marklab-cohort; cohort CLI; selected project routes; integrated study/pathology workflows. Other spatial/model endpoints require explicit patient-level aggregation and compatible tables.
uses: Compare multivariate or functional tissue signatures
cohort_inference.limits: Cells are not cohort replicates. Exchangeability and covariate/block designs must match sampling. Two-group Max-T has scoped Experimental evidence; other designs remain Research. Nonsignificance is not equivalence.

does: Conjugate normal mean and Gaussian patient hierarchy
Ordinal/group-site/nonproportional ordinal models and whole-site holdout
Gaussian crossed/nested effects and variance partition
bayesian_hierarchies.input: Counts, continuous/ordered outcomes and grouping/covariate data with declared priors and fitting controls.
bayesian_hierarchies.output: Posterior effects/uncertainty, model diagnostics and model-specific predictive/sensitivity results.
bayesian_hierarchies.used_by: marklab-bayes models; bayes commands invoke model-specific workers; selected fits have project counterparts. Agreement/SBC/sensitivity exist only for the named command variants.
bayesian_hierarchies.limits: Research evidence is model-specific. Nonconverged fits remain diagnostic. Variance partition is a mean share of random-effect/residual variance, not R-squared or fixed-effect variance.

does: GP regression, multi-output and anisotropic 3-D GP
Variational GP, predictive-process and NNGP approximations
Adaptive polygon-window and nonstationary anisotropic SPDE
bayesian_spatial_fields.input: Spatial outcomes/covariates, coordinates or adjacency, optional mesh, priors and resource constraints.
bayesian_spatial_fields.output: Field/effect predictions, density/likelihood values or fitted posterior/optimization summaries according to the command.
bayesian_spatial_fields.used_by: bayes field/SPDE commands; selected project routes; dense GP/SPDE priors also support multimodal spatial factors.
bayesian_spatial_fields.limits: Some density/build commands evaluate or construct models without fitting. Anisotropic GP needs identifiable axis scales; its inverse-square plug-in metric has physical units. Approximation/mesh assumptions and convergence remain explicit.

does: Covariate-dependent Poisson likelihood/fit and Berman-Turner refinement
Replicated multitype and correlated multitype LGCP
Conditional multitype marks at fixed locations
Geyer saturation and multitype Papangelou intensities
Posterior predictive point patterns and spatial checks
bayesian_point_processes.input: Locations/types/marks, observation windows, covariates/quadrature, replication and priors or declared process parameters.
bayesian_point_processes.output: Likelihood/model specification, posterior intensity/mark/cluster summaries, generated patterns or predictive diagnostics.
bayesian_point_processes.used_by: bayes point-process/build/fit commands; selected project routes cache polygon/replicated models; posterior checks compare generated and observed spatial summaries.
uses: Separate abundance/intensity from conditional mark organization
bayesian_point_processes.limits: Build commands do not imply a completed fit. Gibbs statistics/pseudolikelihood are not a general exact continuous-space Gibbs posterior. Dense Thomas fits can mix slowly; a real-data location-embedding fit did not converge. Research scope remains model-specific.

inference_and_model_checks.input: Declared observations/models or posterior log likelihoods; priors, simulation scenarios, quadrature and diagnostic criteria.
inference_and_model_checks.output: Approximate/posterior summaries, LOO scores/Pareto diagnostics, calibration ranks/coverage, agreement/sensitivity or predictive discrepancies.
inference_and_model_checks.used_by: bayes named inference and check commands wrap specific models; validation tools are not generic proof of every model's accuracy.
inference_and_model_checks.limits: Sampling convergence, backend agreement, SBC and public-cohort validity are different evidence. An implemented check is not a claim it passed on the user's data.

does: Full, partial and unbalanced fused Gromov-Wasserstein
optimal_transport.input: Source/target masses and feature/cross-costs; FGW adds within-set geometry and declared feature/structure scales.
optimal_transport.output: Couplings/assignments, matched/unmatched mass, objective/convergence and multistart diagnostics.
optimal_transport.used_by: marklab-transport; bayes transport commands; project fused-gromov-wasserstein. Basic Sinkhorn is native; FGW uses POT and partial OT uses SciPy.
uses: Allow partial overlap or changing total mass
optimal_transport.limits: Coupling is not cell identity. FGW is nonconvex and uses multiple starts; unbalanced zero-mass collapse errors. No calibrated biological correspondence test.

prediction.input: Patient-level scores/features/labels with explicit training/calibration/test splits; out-of-fold base predictions for fusion.
prediction.output: Calibrated probabilities/sets/coverage, OOD and abstention decisions, fusion/gating weights and held-out performance diagnostics.
prediction.used_by: marklab-prediction; bayes prediction commands consume declared upstream model outputs. Region retrieval is a separate embedding workflow.
prediction.limits: Coverage/calibration depend on split/exchangeability assumptions. Base predictions must satisfy the declared out-of-fold contract. No demonstrated clinical safety or general real-cohort predictive validity.

does: Read Bruker flex fid/acqu acquisitions (time of flight to m/z) or two-column text spectra
Ordered square-root, Savitzky-Golay, SNIP baseline, total-ion-current and trim steps
Fixed-edge m/z binning with in-order summation
maldi_spectra.input: One Bruker flex spectrum directory (fid with acqu or acqus) or one two-column text spectrum, and a JSON list of preprocessing steps with optional bins.
maldi_spectra.output: Acquisition facts, the preprocessed m/z spectrum and optional binned intensities.
uses: Prepare MALDI-TOF spectra of bacterial isolates for species and susceptibility models
maldi_spectra.limits: HPC, LIFT, PSD and V1.0 CTOF2 calibrations are rejected. One spectrum per run; no peak detection, alignment, replicate averaging, mzML or mzXML. Not spatial.

does: Parquet feature tables (id, numeric features, modality/unit/provenance metadata) from binned MALDI-TOF spectra or any writer
Cross-fitted ensembles of L2-penalised logistic regression with Platt calibration and class-conditional conformal calls
Outer cross-validation of the fitting procedure: AUROC, average precision, Brier score, reliability, very major/major/abstention rates
Saved models that predict only feature tables made the same way
maldi_ast_prediction.input: A Parquet feature table (one row per isolate or specimen), a CSV label table (ID, antibiotic category, optional species and group), and a JSON configuration of categories and fitting settings.
maldi_ast_prediction.output: A model file (feature schema, settings, ensemble, calibration) and an evaluation report; predict-ast writes each row's calibrated probability, conformal p-values and call.
maldi_ast_prediction.used_by: marklab microbio feature-table, fit-ast and predict-ast; marklab-prediction LogisticProblem, fit_and_evaluate_logistic_ensemble and PlattScaling.
uses: Estimate how well MALDI-TOF spectra or other features predict resistance for one antibiotic
Predict resistance for new isolates with calibrated probabilities and abstaining calls
maldi_ast_prediction.limits: One antibiotic per fit; L2 penalty only; categories taken as given (no MIC or breakpoint interpretation); no specimen-to-isolate linking or modality fusion; grouped random folds only. Not a clinical susceptibility test.

does: Vessel-source transport in a static flow field
simulation.input: Windows/grids, initial states, equations/parameters, boundary/numerical settings, seeds and budgets.
simulation.output: Synthetic cells, trajectories/states, solver diagnostics or weighted summary losses.
simulation.used_by: marklab-simulation and simulate CLI; the Fisher-KPP solver is directly consumed by growth-front SBI. Point-process simulators are also exposed under bayes.
simulation.limits: Equations and parameters are hypotheses; summary matching does not identify or validate a mechanism in real tissue.

does: Periodic 2-D conserved Cahn-Hilliard evolution with double-well free energy
Stabilized semi-implicit Fourier step using the finite-difference Laplacian spectrum
Stepwise mean/mass and discrete free-energy checks with bounded work
phase_field_domains.input: Initial row-major scalar field, spacing, mobility, bulk/gradient energy coefficients, time step, horizon and recording/work bounds.
phase_field_domains.output: Initial/final fields, trajectory summaries, conservation, free energy and solver diagnostics.
uses: Study declared segregation/coarsening and interface-relaxation hypotheses
Generate synthetic spatial fields for method checks
phase_field_domains.limits: Periodic conserved dynamics with no growth, death, advection or fitted biological parameters. Mass conservation and energy decay establish solver behavior, not a tissue mechanism. No automatic phase-field SBI route.

simulation_based_inference.input: Observed summaries, Fisher-KPP initial state/design, prior/tolerance and simulation/particle budgets.
simulation_based_inference.output: Accepted/weighted posterior draws, support decisions, calibration or predictive checks.
simulation_based_inference.used_by: marklab-sbi -> marklab-simulation Fisher-KPP; bayes growth-front inference commands; project smc-abc-growth-front caches the SMC route.
uses: Check whether observations lie within simulator support
Assess recovery and posterior fit on synthetic controls
simulation_based_inference.limits: Current workflows are specific simulator/summary contracts. Similar summaries may come from different parameters or mechanisms.

does: Neural point-process intensity and categorical marks
neural_models.input: Point patterns/windows, patient splits/context or declared simulations/priors with architecture/training/resource settings.
neural_models.output: Intensity/mark predictions, generated patterns, posterior summaries or generative diagnostics.
neural_models.used_by: neural CLI orchestrates locked JAX/torch/sbi or model-specific workers.
neural_models.limits: This family does not train image encoders. Synthetic checks do not establish tissue posterior coverage or real-cohort performance.

causal_designs.input: Treatment/outcomes, units/clusters, covariates, interference graph and explicit identification/design assumptions.
causal_designs.output: Effects/exposures, sensitivity curves/bounds, information gain or selected acquisitions/power diagnostics.
causal_designs.used_by: marklab-causal and causal CLI; selected project randomized-interference/gaussian-eig routes; advanced designs use Python workers.
causal_designs.limits: Requires the stated randomization/exposure/observational identification assumptions. Tissue association alone does not satisfy them.

does: Permutation association of phylogenetic and spatial distances
longitudinal.input: Repeated observations with transition/noise model, nonlinear/particle settings or clone/tree and spatial distances.
longitudinal.output: Predicted/filtered/smoothed states and uncertainty, likelihood diagnostics or distance-association inference.
longitudinal.used_by: marklab-longitudinal; longitudinal CLI; project longitudinal-kalman-smooth. Registered 3-D timepoint change is a separate spatial3d flow.
longitudinal.limits: Conditional on the declared dynamical/noise model; no real repeated-patient clinical validation or same-cell tracking.

does: Normalized weighted means and two-pass covariance
numerical_foundation.input: Finite vectors/matrices/weights or aligned observed/null curves with explicit size/work limits.
numerical_foundation.output: Stable numerical summaries/solutions or explicit singular/unavailable failures; global-envelope depths/bounds/p-values.
numerical_foundation.used_by: marklab-numerics underlies spatial sums, covariance, graph/kernel/kriging computations and ERL inference; numerics stable-primitives exposes selected operations.
uses: Custom Rust analyses using the same numerical policies
Method checks against known small problems
numerical_foundation.limits: Primitives are not separate scientific models; numerical stability is not evidence of biological validity.

does: Typed workflow DAG and local scheduler
Compatible result caching and dependent invalidation
durable_execution_and_policy.input: Declared nodes, dependencies, input artifacts, algorithm/runtime identity, seeds and resource limits; policy decisions consume declared evidence flags.
durable_execution_and_policy.output: Stored artifacts, node/run/cache/recovery status, completed reports or policy decisions.
durable_execution_and_policy.used_by: project's explicit command subset, study run and public workflow nodes; backend doctor checks the installed worker runtime.
durable_execution_and_policy.limits: No universal automatic pipeline connecting all commands. Cached execution and declared policy flags do not promote scientific validity. The scheduler is local, not a distributed service.

does: GUDHI, scikit-image, POT, SimpleITK, MOFA, CCA and neural workers
Isolated process environment and bounded execution
Compatible saved-result reuse without new backend execution
python_backend_runtime.input: Worker assets, locked environment, serialized requests and explicit runtime/cache configuration.
python_backend_runtime.output: Identity-checked worker results, version/runtime diagnostics or explicit failure.
python_backend_runtime.used_by: Model-specific CLI orchestration and durable project nodes. MARKLAB_RUNTIME_ROOT, MARKLAB_PYTHON, MARKLAB_BACKEND_CACHE and MARKLAB_BACKEND_PATH configure execution; MARKLAB_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_BACKEND_EXECUTION blocks new launches.
uses: Run selected external scientific implementations reproducibly
python_backend_runtime.limits: Doctor checks installation/versions, not numerical accuracy, model suitability or GPU support. Linux is the CI reference; all families retain their own evidence and platform limits.

does: SPACE census of radius discs around seed cells: object-class percentages, class-linked scalar means and independent scalar means
cisMI: rank every ensemble of up to depth variables (default 3) by co-information against shuffled-member randomized censuses

transMI: rank every ensemble by the modularity of each grouping factor on a specimen similarity network built from symmetric KL divergences of smoothed joint distributions, against shuffled divergences
Plot data: one or two variables' disc values or smoothed joint distribution, and a cisMI or transMI result's kept ensembles, variable scores or one ensemble across radii

Patterns: a self-organizing-map path through an ensemble's focal discs with each variable's rolling mean and band, and enrichment against a reference group or a randomized census; maps of each cell's region of that path
Diversity: each specimen's class or scalar composition and Shannon entropy, and beta diversity across parent classes or pattern regions; suggested disc counts for a desired coverage
space_ensembles.input: A marklab.space_request naming inline specimens, a multiplex study recipe or one CellViT H&E classification CSV per specimen, the object channels and scalars, grouping factors, and radii, disc counts and seeds.
space_ensembles.output: Disc census tables; per specimen and radius, every ensemble's observed and randomized co-information, CisMI, Z, SPACE's normal P with BH adjustment, a Monte Carlo P and each variable's binning range; per radius, ensemble and grouping factor, transMI, its shuffled-null mean and SD, Z, SPACE's one-sided normal P with BH adjustment and a Monte Carlo P. Distribution views and rankings of those results; pattern curves along a learned path and per-cell path regions; compositions, alpha and beta diversity; suggested sample sizes.
space_ensembles.used_by: marklab::space and the marklab space describe/census/cis/trans/dist/rank/pattern/map/diversity/suggest commands.
uses: Find three-way and higher cell-type and marker co-patterning that pairwise statistics miss
Find ensembles whose patterning separates clinical or experimental groups of specimens
Use CellViT classifications or multiplex panels directly as SPACE objects and scalars
space_ensembles.limits: Port of R SPACE's table workflow (commit 94f0a0f), including three-dimensional tables, plus label and intensity rasters (8- and 16-bit greyscale PNG; TIFF pending a wsi-rs update) sampled at cells or censused as pixel grids with SPACE's patch null. The randomized census tests departure from a well-mixed tissue, not direct interaction; discs overlap; rare variables have unstable bin grids; a pattern's path is an ordering of discs, and its map depends on the seed. transMI compares each specimen's distribution on its own range, and its null shuffles only the pairwise divergences, so few specimens give a coarse null.

mathematical_methods.scope: Explicit mathematical engines, independent of biological outputs. Equations state core constructions; each implementation retains its own normalization, observation, inference and resource contract.

fourier_spectral_analysis.equation: P(k) = |sum_i (m_i - mean(m)) exp(-i k dot x_i)|^2 / n
fourier_spectral_analysis.role: Cell-mark organization across spatial frequency and direction; shell power is compared with label-permutation spectra. Outputs include low-frequency excess, resolvable characteristic scale and anisotropy. A tapered raster FFT is a separate gridding diagnostic.

graph_fourier_and_diffusion.equation: L = U Lambda U^T; graph coefficients = U^T f; f_t = exp(-t L) f
graph_fourier_and_diffusion.role: Resolve features into graph frequencies and propagation scales; wavelets/scattering extend the multiscale description. Graph definition and Laplacian normalization are declared.

bayesian_inference.equation: p(theta | data) proportional to p(data | theta) p(theta)
bayesian_inference.role: Hierarchical effects, spatial fields, point processes and mark models with posterior uncertainty. Full posterior sampling, approximate fits and model-construction-only commands are distinct.

supervised_feature_combination.equation: beta = argmin_b ||(y_train - mean(y_train)) - X_train_standardized b||^2 + lambda ||b||^2
supervised_feature_combination.role: The existing complementarity workflow compares baseline, cell, patch, neighbor and measured feature blocks using ridge regression and nested patient-held-out validation. Standardization uses training rows.
supervised_feature_combination.h_optimus_cellvit_connection: A caller may supply H-optimus patch summaries, CellViT embedding/class summaries and spatial/Fourier features in compatible patient blocks. Pooling, dimensionality reduction and that model-specific mapping are not automatically implemented; no fixed H-optimus/CellViT fusion equation is configured.

multiresolution_spatial_factor_model.equation: Y_ij ~ Normal([sum_s B_s A_s W_s^T]_ij, sigma^2)
multiresolution_spatial_factor_model.role: Fit shared continuous-feature structure through declared spatial bases B_s, coefficients A_s and loadings W_s at multiple scales. Gaussian priors; MAP fitting with Laplace uncertainty. This is separate from supervised ridge and from full MCMC.

fixed_multiscale_kernels.equation: K(a,b) = sum_s w_s k(z_a,s, z_b,s), with positive prespecified weights summing to one
fixed_multiscale_kernels.role: Combine similarities across declared spatial scales; report drop-one-scale sensitivity. Existing fixed scale weights are not learned multimodal kernel fusion.

optimal_transport.equation: Balanced entropic OT: minimize <C,P> + epsilon sum_ij P_ij(log P_ij - 1), subject to P >= 0 and declared marginals
optimal_transport.role: Align weighted distributions; FGW additionally compares within-set geometry. Partial and unbalanced variants change the mass constraints/penalties. Couplings do not establish cell identity.

gibbs_style_mark_interactions.equation: p(z_i = k | neighbor types) = softmax_k(intercept + neighbor_counts_i times potential^T)
gibbs_style_mark_interactions.role: The conditional multitype model estimates symmetric type-interaction potentials using a categorical pseudolikelihood with Gaussian priors. Separate finite binary Gibbs and Strauss/Geyer paths also exist; these are not causal interaction estimates.

topology_and_connectivity.construction: Track connected components and loops over a distance/filtration scale; summarize persistence and graph connectivity transitions.
topology_and_connectivity.role: Measure structural organization beyond counts and pairwise distances. Existing connectivity includes largest-component fraction, susceptibility and boundary spanning; finite tissue is not proof of an infinite-system phase transition.

equations: H(p) = -sum_k p_k log(p_k)
I(X;Y) = E log[p(X,Y)/(p(X)p(Y))]
information_theory.role: Composition diversity and pairwise nonlinear dependence with method-specific logarithm/normalization and spatial nulls. The separate discrete I_min workflow now decomposes two-source information into redundancy, unique terms and synergy.

reaction_diffusion_and_interfaces.example_equation: Fisher-KPP: partial_t u = D partial_xx u + r u(1-u/K)
reaction_diffusion_and_interfaces.role: Declared growth, competition, transport and interface hypotheses; native simulators connect to selected ABC and synthetic-likelihood inference. Spatial resemblance alone does not identify the generating dynamics.

equations: L(r)=sqrt(K(r)/pi); g(r)=K_prime(r)/(2 pi r) under the stationary isotropic 2-D definition
point_pattern_second_order.role: K accumulates neighbors; g describes annular scale. Estimation uses the declared edge correction, intensity and finite-count/null convention. Directed cross-type forms preserve source/target roles.

equations: G(r)=P(point-to-nearest-point distance <= r)
F(r)=P(probe-to-nearest-point distance <= r)
J(r)=(1-G(r))/(1-F(r)) on supported radii
nearest_neighbor_and_voids.role: Separate observed-cell crowding from empty-space structure; reduced-sample border support and probe design matter.

equations: Continuous normalized mark correlation compares mean pair products in a distance bin with the declared mark-mean product
Soft neighborhood composition averages complete class-probability vectors over declared neighbors
marked_pairs_and_neighborhoods.role: Hard labels, ordinal levels, probabilities and continuous marks have different contracts. Categorical co-occurrence, exact enrichment moments, mark connection, weighted K and conservative top-1 bounds are distinct methods.

equations: I=(n/sum_ij w_ij) sum_ij w_ij z_i z_j / sum_i z_i^2
C=((n-1)/(2 sum_ij w_ij)) sum_ij w_ij (x_i-x_j)^2 / sum_i z_i^2; z_i=x_i-mean(x)
autocorrelation.role: Global Moran/Geary describe dependence under explicit weights. Local scalar/multivariate versions have their own scaling, isolate and permutation conventions.

equations: gamma(h)=mean_pairs_at_h [(z_i-z_j)^2]/2
Ordinary kriging predicts sum_i w_i z_i with sum_i w_i=1 under a declared variogram
variograms_covariance_and_kriging.role: Scalar/vector/projected semivariograms and cross-covariance quantify distance-dependent representation changes; kriging is a separate interpolation model with held-out block checks.

equations: density = eligible_count / observed_area
log ratio = log(declared numerator composition / declared denominator composition)
interface profile = declared measurement summarized by signed or unsigned physical distance band
composition_geometry_and_maps.role: Fractions, density, balances, entropy, exact polygon overlaps, interface contact, fragmentation, curvature, skeletons, budding and nuclear shape are separate tissue measurements. Zero/empty support remains explicit.

equations: psi_k(i)=mean_neighbors exp(i k theta_ij)
Box-count slope estimates -d log N(epsilon)/d log epsilon over declared scales
Landy-Szalay xi=(DD-2DR+RR)/RR with the implemented pair normalization
packing_gaps_and_density_structure.role: Bond orientation uses neighbor bonds, whereas nematic order uses measured cell axes. Morisita quadrats, lacunarity and structure-factor H/alpha summarize other aspects of packing and gaps.

equations: Q=<2 n n^T-I>_w; S=sqrt(Q_xx^2+Q_xy^2)
charge=(sum wrapped differences of doubled director phase)/(4 pi)
nematic_tensor_and_defects.role: Screen resolved +/-1/2 winding on complete-support grid plaquettes. A static director field is a shape descriptor, not a measurement of active stress.

equations: I_spec(t;A)=KL[p(A|t)||p(A)]
R=sum_t p(t) min(I_spec(t;A),I_spec(t;B))
U_A=I(T;A)-R; U_B=I(T;B)-R; synergy=I(T;A,B)-I(T;A)-I(T;B)+R
partial_information_decomposition.role: Empirical discrete Williams-Beer I_min in bits, with declared categories and no pseudocounts. Its redundancy definition has the independent-bits/joint-target limitation described in the method document.

equations: K=sum_m alpha_m K_m; alpha_m>=0; sum_m alpha_m=1
(K_train+lambda I)a=y_train-mean(y_train); prediction=mean(y_train)+K_test,train a
multiple_kernel_learning.role: Nonnegative sums preserve positive semidefiniteness. Native workflow selects a finite simplex grid and ridge penalty inside patient training folds; weights are predictive tuning parameters.

equations: Y_m approximately Z W_m^T plus model-specific private effects and observation noise
latent_factor_models.role: PCCA, Bayesian PCCA, MOFA, hierarchical/spatial/tensor/multiresolution and dropout-robust models differ in likelihood, constraints, missingness and fitting method. A factor is not automatically a named phenotype.

equations: f~Normal(0,K_theta) for covariance-based Gaussian fields
p(f) proportional to exp(-f^T Q f/2) on the supported subspace for precision-based Gaussian fields
gaussian_spatial_fields.role: GP, multi-output/variational/predictive-process/NNGP, CAR/SAR/GMRF/BYM and SPDE methods choose different covariance, precision, adjacency and approximation contracts.

equations: Poisson log likelihood = sum_i log lambda(x_i) - integral_window lambda(x) dx
LGCP: log lambda(x) includes a latent Gaussian field
spatial_point_process_likelihoods.role: Exact-window/quadrature exposure, replicate hierarchy, type-specific intensity and conditional mark interactions are modeled explicitly. Strauss/Geyer and Thomas/Matern cluster mechanisms are different process families.

equations: g(E[y_ij])=X_ij beta + patient/slide/site effects under a declared likelihood and link
hierarchical_observation_models.role: Gaussian/Student-t, count, beta-binomial, composition, hurdle and ordinal models suit different observations. Partial pooling does not make repeated cells independent patients.

equations: Monte Carlo tail p=(1+number of null statistics at least as extreme)/(B+1), with method-specific tails/ties
Max-T compares endpoint statistics with the permutation maximum over the declared family
permutation_envelopes_and_multiplicity.role: ERL compares aligned curves jointly over eligible scales. Paired, stratified, blocked, cluster and Freedman-Lane designs encode different exchangeability assumptions; correction does not cover unrecorded exploratory searches.

equations: Energy distance and kernel MMD compare declared multivariate distributions
TOST/equivalence evaluates a prespecified practical margin rather than treating nonsignificance as equality
patient_effects_distances_and_equivalenc.role: Functional L2, multivariate distances, patient/hierarchical bootstrap and fixed/random-effects synthesis extend scalar group comparisons. Cell-level and patient-level uncertainty differ.

equations: Conformal sets use a calibration-score quantile under the declared grouping/exchangeability design
Mixture prediction combines expert outputs with declared context-dependent gate weights
prediction_calibration_and_support.role: Grouped conformal prediction, calibrated late fusion, predictive stacking, OOD support and abstention need distinct training/calibration/test roles. These are separate from latent-factor or kernel feature fusion.

equations: Dirichlet energy=f^T L f
Edge flow=gradient component+curl component+harmonic component on the declared complex
graph_energy_motifs_and_hodge.role: Group centrality, typed triangles, hypergraphs and heterogeneous message passing retain the graph/complex definition. They do not automatically infer biological communication or communities.

equations: x_t=A x_(t-1)+process_noise; y_t=H x_t+measurement_noise for the linear-Gaussian model
longitudinal_state_space.role: Kalman filtering/RTS smoothing and nonlinear/particle variants condition on a declared dynamic/noise model. Phylogenetic-spatial distance association is a separate permutation workflow.

equations: Potential outcomes can be indexed by own treatment and declared neighborhood exposure
Expected information gain averages a future posterior-to-prior information change under the acquisition model
causal_interference_and_design.role: Randomized interference, observational cross-fitting, Manski/Rosenbaum sensitivity and active design require their identification assumptions. An interesting single-slide association does not supply them.

equations: F[phi]=integral [A(phi^2-1)^2/4 + kappa|grad phi|^2/2] dx
partial_t phi=M Laplacian(mu); mu=A(phi^3-phi)-kappa Laplacian(phi)
phase_field_free_energy.role: The native periodic 2-D conserved simulator checks the corresponding discrete energy and mass after each accepted step. Fitting tissue dynamics and growth/source terms are outside this workflow.

equations: ABC accepts or weights simulator parameters by a declared distance between simulated and observed summaries
Synthetic likelihood models a distribution of summary statistics conditional on simulator parameters
simulation_based_and_neural_inference.role: Rejection/SMC ABC, synthetic likelihood and neural SBI have different approximation/calibration needs. Existing growth-front routes are wired to the simulator; new phase-field outputs are not automatically an SBI input.

equations: logsumexp(x)=m+log sum_i exp(x_i-m), m=max(x)
Cholesky and triangular solves operate on admitted finite matrices
numerical_primitives.role: Compensated sums, stable covariance and bounded solvers support the scientific methods. They are not standalone evidence of biological validity.

equations: b = min(floor(((ss + 1) / 10)^(1 / depth)), max_bins) equally spaced bins per variable over its observed and randomized range
Co-information of an ensemble S is the sum over nonempty subsets T of (-1)^(|T| - 1) H(T), with plug-in joint entropy H in bits
CisMI = observed co-information minus the mean over randomized censuses; Z = CisMI / null standard deviation

transMI: per specimen, a Chao-Jost-smoothed joint distribution over b^k cells on its own range; D = mean of KL(p||q) and KL(q||p) in bits; similarity 1 - D / max D; Q = sum over groups c of e_c / m - (K_c / m)^2 on the directed network with unit self-loops
ensemble_co_information.role: SPACE's binned, multi-way information measure on disc compositions. It is distinct from the KSG mutual information and two-source partial information decomposition in structure descriptors.

multimodal_integration.common_unit: First choose a common biological unit and exact joins: cells inside patches/regions, matched coordinates after registration, and finally patient-level rows for endpoint prediction.

feature_blocks.H: Upstream H-optimus or another patch encoder: explicit patch coordinates, support, pooling and patient aggregation.
feature_blocks.C: Upstream CellViT or another cell encoder: identity-aligned cell vectors and declared patient/region summaries.
feature_blocks.Q: Hard classes or complete class probabilities: composition, density and neighborhood/mixing summaries with missingness rules.
feature_blocks.S: Spatial summaries: K/g, co-occurrence, Moran/variograms, Fourier bands, architecture, graph/topology or nematic features with common physical scales.
feature_blocks.M: Measured assay/clinical covariates with explicit observed status; predicted molecular quantities remain labeled predictions.

routes.construction: X_p = [baseline_p, H_p, C_p, Q_p, S_p, M_p]; ridge minimizes squared error plus lambda times squared coefficient norm after training-only scaling.
routes.implementation: multimodal compare-models / bayes test-cell-patch-complementarity; map blocks into its declared baseline/cell/patch/neighbor/measured design.
routes.question: Does each added block improve outer-patient predictions over a simpler model?

routes.construction: K = sum_m alpha_m K_m, alpha_m >= 0, sum_m alpha_m = 1; (K_train + lambda I)a = y_train - mean(y_train).
routes.implementation: multimodal kernel-fusion; named modality blocks, linear/RBF kernels, nested patient folds.
routes.question: Does a combination of modality similarities improve held-out continuous-target prediction over equal weights or any single modality?

routes.construction: For a chosen factor model, observations are generated from shared/private latent factors and modality loadings; spatial versions add declared bases or GP/SPDE priors.
routes.implementation: multimodal pcca, bayesian-pcca, mofa, matrix-factor, hierarchical-factor, spatial-matrix-factor, tensor-factor, spatial-latent-factor, multiresolution-factor, dropout-robust and joint-pathology.
routes.question: Which patterns vary together across declared modalities? This does not itself establish endpoint prediction.

routes.construction: Use declared held-out probabilities/log predictive densities for late fusion, predictive stacking or context-dependent expert gates.
routes.question: Do independently generated expert predictions improve calibrated held-out prediction?

routes.construction: I(T;H,C) = redundancy + unique_H + unique_C + synergy under the explicitly chosen discrete I_min definition.
routes.implementation: numerics partial-information-decomposition after prespecified or training-only low-dimensional discretization.
routes.question: How does this estimator allocate empirical target information? It is separate from proving added predictive value.

multimodal_integration.training_boundary: Patient splits must precede feature selection, dimension reduction, scaling and supervised tuning. The kernel command handles its own scaling and tuning, but cannot repair leakage introduced upstream.
multimodal_integration.current_wiring: The component workflows exist. There is no built-in one-command H-optimus-to-CellViT-to-spatial-to-patient model pipeline or universal result-file concatenator.
multimodal_integration.recommended_start: Use a small prespecified patient feature table and existing ridge block comparison first; add the learned kernel comparison when nonlinear similarity is part of the question. On a single slide without independent targets, start with descriptive maps and representations rather than supervised kernel fitting.

interactions.flow: Upstream segmentation/classification -> calibrated cells + observed window -> marked analysis -> batch/prepost
interactions.note: Upstream image modeling is external; batch shares configuration, and prepost compares completed compatible analyses.

interactions.flow: H&E + IHC + landmarks -> registration -> fused cells -> graph -> enrichment/cross-curves/territories
interactions.note: The basic multimodal pipeline; registration quality affects downstream interpretation.

interactions.flow: Multiplex cells -> per-marker slide autocorrelation -> patient means -> Max-T report
interactions.note: study runs and caches the complete chain; each patient counts once.

interactions.flow: Typed patient slides -> composition/grid sensitivity or intensity-adjusted curves -> patient-group inference
interactions.note: pathology composition and spatial-study use different pooling and null designs.

interactions.flow: Annotated structures + cells -> interface distances/neighborhood composition/local Moran -> maps
interactions.note: pathology maps produces physical-coordinate SVG/GeoJSON layers.

interactions.flow: Epithelium + declared regions -> bulk/front/bands -> architecture/nuclei/buds/spot coverage
interactions.note: pathology architecture; spot-expression joins occur downstream using explicit spot IDs.

interactions.flow: Cell/patch vectors + exact links -> multiscale support -> spatial features or held-out complementarity
interactions.note: Artifacts and individual methods exist; callers choose compatible feature definitions and patient splits.

interactions.flow: Section/graph/topology/embedding features -> patient endpoints -> cohort/Bayesian/prediction models
interactions.note: Requires declared endpoint construction and aggregation; arbitrary output JSON is not an automatic next-command input.

interactions.flow: Growth-front simulator -> ABC/synthetic likelihood -> posterior-predictive and support checks
interactions.note: The SBI growth-front routes directly call the native simulator.

interactions.flow: Registered serial/longitudinal sections -> coordinate uncertainty -> voxel-window 3-D K/change
interactions.note: Dedicated spatial3d routes propagate the declared registration uncertainty.

interactions.flow: Scientific command -> admitted node -> local artifact store -> compatible cache reuse
interactions.note: Only listed project routes and public workflow nodes have this execution path.

interactions.flow: Measured nuclear/cell axes + window -> nematic Q/director field -> resolved half defects -> region/front or patient summaries
interactions.note: The orientation command does not automatically join architecture or perform cohort inference.

interactions.flow: Patient modality feature blocks + continuous target + declared folds -> nested kernel/ridge selection -> outer predictions and equal/single baselines
interactions.note: No raw encoder inference or cell/patch/slide pooling is performed by kernel-fusion.

interactions.flow: Two declared discrete sources + target joint counts -> I_min redundancy/unique/synergy
interactions.note: Separate from held-out predictive complementarity; no automatic continuous embedding PID.

interactions.flow: Initial scalar grid + free-energy parameters -> conserved phase-field simulation -> fields/energy/conservation summaries
interactions.note: Comparison to tissue spectra/interfaces needs explicit observation and aggregation; no automatic parameter fitting/SBI chain.

research_extensions.scope: The four proposed extensions are now implemented bounded Research workflows. Their primary inventory entries are in capabilities and their equations are in mathematical_methods; biological usefulness remains an empirical question.

learned_multimodal_kernels.priority: First candidate for supervised multimodal integration
learned_multimodal_kernels.equation: K = alpha_H K_Hoptimus + alpha_C K_CellViT + alpha_Q K_classes + alpha_S K_spatial; alpha >= 0, sum(alpha) = 1
learned_multimodal_kernels.theorem: Nonnegative sums of positive-semidefinite kernels remain positive-semidefinite. Under representer-theorem conditions, a regularized predictor has a finite expansion f(x) = sum_j a_j K(x_j,x).
learned_multimodal_kernels.application: Keep model embeddings, class composition and spatial signatures in their own feature spaces while combining their similarities at a common patient/sample level. Choose kernel scaling and learn weights inside patient-held-out training; Bayesian formulations can model uncertainty.
learned_multimodal_kernels.current_status: Implemented: multimodal kernel-fusion performs nested patient cross-validation for convex linear/RBF kernel weights and ridge penalties, with equal-weight and single-modality comparisons. Finite simplex grid; continuous targets; no Bayesian uncertainty or automated upstream pooling. See docs/multimodal-kernel-fusion.md.
learned_multimodal_kernels.test_of_value: Compare with existing standardized ridge and each input block alone on identical patient folds; evaluate held-out performance/calibration and sensitivity to correlated kernels. Kernel weights are not causal importance.

nematic_orientation_and_defects.priority: Candidate for architecture and invasive-front research
equations: Q(x) = <2 n n^T - I>_weight in a declared local neighborhood
S(x) = |<exp(2 i theta)>|
nematic_orientation_and_defects.application: Map local alignment, disorder and orientation-field defects; test associations with supplied architecture classes, budding or front distance.
nematic_orientation_and_defects.current_status: Implemented: numerics nematic-orientation computes weighted global/local Q and S, a regular-grid director field and screened +/-1/2 defects with explicit boundary, support, order and branch-ambiguity statuses. See docs/nematic-orientation.md.
nematic_orientation_and_defects.test_of_value: Check known synthetic orientation fields, segmentation/angular uncertainty and independent tissue measurements. Nuclear axes are an imperfect proxy for cell orientation; static slides alone cannot establish active stresses or a causal extrusion mechanism.

partial_information_decomposition.priority: Exploratory complementarity analysis after a reliable predictive baseline
partial_information_decomposition.equation: I(Y; H,C) = redundant_information + unique_H + unique_C + synergistic_information
partial_information_decomposition.application: Ask whether H-optimus and CellViT provide duplicated, distinct or jointly useful information about a declared endpoint; spatial summaries could enter an explicitly chosen multivariate extension.
partial_information_decomposition.current_status: Implemented: numerics partial-information-decomposition computes discrete two-source Williams-Beer I_min from a declared joint-count table, in bits. No automatic binning, bias correction, significance or causal interpretation. See docs/partial-information-decomposition.md.
partial_information_decomposition.test_of_value: Select a stated redundancy definition, use reduced representations and patient-level sampling, and verify known redundancy/synergy controls. Definitions and estimators differ; high-dimensional small-cohort estimates can be unstable.

phase_field_domain_models.priority: Mechanistic extension only with a concrete domain-formation question and temporal/experimental constraints
equations: F[phi] = integral [f(phi) + (kappa/2)|grad phi|^2] dx
Conserved dynamics: partial_t phi = div(M grad(delta F/delta phi))
phase_field_domain_models.application: Explore whether a declared segregation/coarsening model can reproduce domain scales, interface geometry and spectra. A growing/dying tissue needs an explicitly justified source term or different conservation law.
phase_field_domain_models.current_status: Implemented: simulate phase-field evolves periodic 2-D Cahn-Hilliard dynamics with a stabilized semi-implicit Fourier solver, bounded work, and stepwise mass/free-energy checks. No fitted biological dynamics or growth/source terms. See docs/phase-field.md.
phase_field_domain_models.test_of_value: Require numerical conservation/free-energy checks and distinguish hypotheses using time courses or perturbations; a single static match cannot identify the dynamics.
